title: Prediction Intervals & Probabilistic Forecasting
interviewAnswer: A point forecast hides uncertainty. Probabilistic forecasting estimates quantiles or a full predictive distribution so decisions can reflect asymmetric risk and service levels.
keyPoints: Prediction interval includes future observation uncertainty.
why: Prediction Intervals & Probabilistic Forecasting appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Prediction interval includes future observation uncertainty.
deepDive: A point forecast hides uncertainty. Probabilistic forecasting estimates quantiles or a full predictive distribution so decisions can reflect asymmetric risk and service levels. Quantile loss evaluates conditional quantiles. Calibration and sharpness both matter. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Inventory planning may use the 90th percentile demand forecast rather than the mean to meet a service target.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

How would you validate or debug Prediction Intervals & Probabilistic Forecasting in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
